suggestions.title: Design a cue card
suggestions.action: Write the habit on a sticky note and put it somewhere unavoidable.
suggestions.rationale: Environmental cues are more reliable triggers than relying on memory alone.

suggestions.title: Reduce to 2 minutes
suggestions.action: Commit to only a 2-minute version when motivation is low.
suggestions.rationale: Starting is the hardest part — a tiny version almost always grows.

suggestions.title: Celebrate with a small gesture
suggestions.action: Say 'yes!' or do a fist pump when done — however small it feels.
suggestions.rationale: Positive emotion immediately after a behaviour strengthens the neural loop.

suggestions.title: Find an accountability partner
suggestions.action: Share your goal with someone and check in weekly.
suggestions.rationale: We naturally adopt habits that feel expected or normal in our social circle.

suggestions.title: Use a habit tracker
suggestions.action: Add a visible checkbox or tally to your daily routine.
suggestions.rationale: Tracking creates a visual streak that motivates you to maintain consistency.

suggestions.title: Connect to identity
suggestions.action: Before starting, remind yourself: 'This is who I am becoming.'
suggestions.rationale: Linking a habit to identity makes the behaviour intrinsically motivating.

suggestions.title: Hide the trigger
suggestions.action: Remove the primary cue from sight or easy reach.
suggestions.rationale: What you see you do — removing the cue breaks the automatic response.

suggestions.title: Reframe the reward
suggestions.action: Notice how you feel an hour after the behaviour — is it worth it?
suggestions.rationale: Delayed reflection erodes the perceived value of the unwanted habit.

suggestions.title: Add friction at the source
suggestions.action: Put your phone in a drawer or use an app blocker during off-hours.
suggestions.rationale: Increasing friction reduces the automatic pull of any trigger.

suggestions.title: Use social accountability
suggestions.action: Tell someone your goal so that breaking it carries a real social cost.
suggestions.rationale: Social accountability makes non-compliance uncomfortable — a powerful deterrent.

suggestions.title: Use a commitment device
suggestions.action: Set up a rule, timer, or app blocker in advance while your resolve is strong.
suggestions.rationale: Binding your future self removes the need for in-the-moment willpower.

suggestions.title: Redesign your environment
suggestions.action: Rearrange your space so the temptation is no longer in the default path.
suggestions.rationale: Environment design is more reliable than willpower.

suggestions.title: Remove one friction step
suggestions.action: Identify the most annoying setup step and eliminate it permanently.
suggestions.rationale: Each friction point is an exit ramp — remove as many as you can.

suggestions.title: Reward completion immediately
suggestions.action: Give yourself a small treat right after completing the habit.
suggestions.rationale: Immediate rewards wire the brain to associate the habit with pleasure.

suggestions.title: Temptation bundling
suggestions.action: Pair this habit with something you genuinely enjoy, like a podcast or coffee.
suggestions.rationale: Combining a 'want' with a 'should' makes the habit much more appealing.

suggestions.rationale: Linking a habit to identity makes the behaviour intrinsically motivating.

suggestions.title: Use a commitment device
suggestions.action: Set up a rule, timer, or app blocker in advance while your resolve is strong.
suggestions.rationale: Binding your future self removes the need for in-the-moment willpower.

suggestions.title: Create a personal consequence
suggestions.action: Set a small, self-imposed penalty for each slip.
suggestions.rationale: Attaching a mild cost to slips shifts the satisfaction calculus against the behaviour.

suggestions.title: Schedule it like a meeting
suggestions.action: Block time on your calendar and treat it as non-negotiable.
suggestions.rationale: What gets scheduled gets done — ambiguity is the enemy of consistency.

suggestions.title: Join a community
suggestions.action: Find a group online or locally that shares this goal.
suggestions.rationale: Belonging to a group that practices the same habit normalises it powerfully.

suggestions.title: Temptation bundling
suggestions.action: Pair this habit with something you genuinely enjoy, like a podcast or coffee.
suggestions.rationale: Combining a 'want' with a 'should' makes the habit much more appealing.

suggestions.title: Celebrate with a small gesture
suggestions.action: Say 'yes!' or do a fist pump when done — however small it feels.
suggestions.rationale: Positive emotion immediately after a behaviour strengthens the neural loop.

suggestions.title: Design a cue card
suggestions.action: Write the habit on a sticky note and put it somewhere unavoidable.
suggestions.rationale: Environmental cues are more reliable triggers than relying on memory alone.
